skill.name: geo-fundamentals
skill.description: Guide and local audit tool for improving web content structure, attribution, and citation readiness across AI-powered search engines.
skill.summary: Assess public web pages and apply GEO practices that make content easier for AI systems to understand and cite.
skill.author: sickn33

content.user_title: Improve Content for AI Search Citations
content.value_statement: Web content often lacks the structure and attribution that AI search engines use when selecting citations. This skill explains GEO practices and audits public web pages for citation readiness.
actual_capabilities: Explains how Generative Engine Optimization differs from traditional search engine optimization.
Provides checklists for citable content, structured data, author attribution, freshness, and crawler access.
Finds likely public pages in HTML, JSX, and TSX files within a local project.
Checks up to 30 pages for JSON-LD, heading structure, author details, and publication dates.
Detects FAQs, lists, tables, entity markup, statistics, and direct-answer patterns.
Reports per-page scores, key issues, and an average citation-readiness score.
limitations: The checker reads source files only and does not crawl deployed sites or query AI search engines.
Pattern detection uses regular expressions and can miss dynamic markup or produce false positives.
All passed checks have equal weight, so the score is not a validated citation probability.
The checker skips Markdown, documentation, tests, configuration files, build directories, and pages beyond the first 30.

use_cases.title: Plan Citable Articles
use_cases.description: Build article briefs with clear definitions, sourced data, expert attribution, FAQs, and structured sections.

use_cases.title: Audit Web Components
use_cases.description: Review HTML, JSX, and TSX pages for structural signals that support AI retrieval and citation.

use_cases.title: Prioritize GEO Improvements
use_cases.description: Compare page scores and reported issues to focus optimization work across a website.

prompt_templates.title: Learn GEO Basics
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain GEO for a beginner. Compare it with SEO and list five content elements that improve AI citation readiness.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when introducing GEO concepts to a content team.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Page Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this page outline for GEO readiness: [outline]. Identify missing definitions, sources, author details, dates, FAQs, lists, and structured data.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use before drafting or updating a public page.

prompt_templates.title: Interpret an Audit
prompt_templates.prompt: Interpret this GEO checker output: [results]. Prioritize the three most important improvements and explain how each addresses a reported issue.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use after running the checker on a local project.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Sitewide GEO Program
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a sitewide GEO improvement plan for [site]. Use [audit results], audience needs, content ownership, implementation effort, and measurable citation-readiness indicators.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for advanced planning across multiple content teams.

output_examples.input: Explain why my article has weak GEO readiness.
output: The page lacks author attribution and publication dates.
No JSON-LD identifies the article or its publisher.
Add direct definitions, sourced statistics, and an FAQ section.

output_examples.input: Prioritize fixes for a page with no H1, no structured data, and one H2.
output: Add one descriptive H1 that states the page topic.
Add relevant JSON-LD with accurate article, author, and date fields.
Create additional H2 sections around distinct user questions.

output_examples.input: Create a GEO checklist for a product comparison article.
output: State the comparison criteria and define important terms.
Use a readable table with current, sourced data.
Name the author, show update dates, and answer common questions.

best_practices: Validate automated findings against rendered pages because dynamic content may not appear in source scans.
Support claims with named, current sources and keep author and date information accurate.
Use the score to prioritize review, then measure real citations and AI-referred traffic separately.
anti_patterns: Do not present unsourced statistics or invented expert quotes to improve apparent authority.
Do not treat a high checker score as proof that an AI engine will cite a page.
Do not add irrelevant schema, repetitive FAQs, or excessive headings only to satisfy checks.

faq.question: What is Generative Engine Optimization?
faq.answer: GEO improves content clarity, structure, attribution, and machine-readable context for retrieval and citation by AI-powered search systems.

faq.question: Which files does the checker inspect?
faq.answer: It inspects likely public pages in HTML, HTM, JSX, and TSX files, while skipping common build, test, documentation, and dependency directories.

faq.question: Does the checker access the internet?
faq.answer: No. The included script reads local project files and prints audit results to the console.

faq.question: Does a high score guarantee AI citations?
faq.answer: No. The score measures detected page elements, not authority, retrieval performance, ranking, or actual citation outcomes.

faq.question: Can it audit a deployed website directly?
faq.answer: No. Provide a local project path containing the website source files.

faq.question: How should teams use the reported issues?
faq.answer: Review each issue against the rendered page, prioritize meaningful content gaps, implement accurate changes, and track real citation results separately.
